run.runNote: Phase 1 Step 1-2 (exploration + candidate extraction query generation) against the CairoSVG_vuln source tree. The CodeQL database CairoSVG-db was created from the same tree (sourceLocationPrefix matches, creation sha 58be378), so file/line evidence below is verified against the database snapshot. Query generation only; no CodeQL execution and no LLM labeling in this step.

target.projectDescription: SVG-to-PNG/PDF/PS/EPS/SVG converter library built on cairocffi. Pure library, not a web service: the attack surface is the SVG document content handed to the public conversion API (svg2png/svg2pdf/svg2svg/svg2ps/svg2eps, Surface.convert) or to the CLI (cairosvg __main__.main). External resources referenced by the input SVG (image href, external SVG, CSS @import) are fetched during rendering, which is the SSRF-relevant behavior.
cwes: CWE-918 primary; pass set also nominally covers CWE-099/610 but this run targets CWE-918

scoring.scale: import/package +0.45, route/decorator/annotation +0.30, runtime/bootstrap +0.20, directory/layout +0.05; threshold primary >= 0.75, secondary 0.50-0.74

framework.selected: none (pure conversion library, no web framework)
framework.notes: CairoSVG is a library, not a Flask/Django/FastAPI service. All framework scores are 0.0 (no web-framework imports anywhere in cairosvg/), so no framework reference is loaded and source/sink shapes are derived from repository evidence per references/python.md and references/patterns.md (language reference path). The real-world SSRF threat model for this library is a host application that converts attacker-supplied SVG documents: the untrusted boundary is the SVG content itself (bytestring/file_obj/url entry parameters) and every external-resource reference the renderer then fetches (image href, external SVG, CSS @import). The host application, not CairoSVG, owns the HTTP surface.

inputBoundaryInventory.summary: Untrusted input reaches CairoSVG as (1) the SVG document itself, via the public conversion API (svg2* bytestring/file_obj/url parameters, Surface.convert) or the CLI (argparse options.input, sys.stdin when input is '-'); (2) references embedded in that document, resolved during rendering: <image> href/xlink:href and xml:base (image.py), tref xlink:href (parser.py text_children), <use> href (defs.py, bounding_box.py), nested/external SVG via Tree(url=...), and CSS @import URLs parsed by tinycss2 (css.py); (3) the caller-supplied url_fetcher callable that replaces the default network fetcher. The only network egress in the entire codebase is urllib.request.urlopen inside url.py fetch(); read_url dispatches to url_fetcher (default fetch) and rewrites schemeless URLs to file://. URL joining/composition (parse_url, urljoin, os.path.join on the base directory) propagates attacker-chosen paths but is not itself network I/O.

cairosvg/url.py:33 'not url.startswith('data:')' - data: URLs are exempted from file normalization in normalize_url; whatever scheme survives parse_url reaches the fetcher as-is

sanitizerObservations: No URL scheme allowlist, host allowlist, private-IP/loopback blocking, or redirect policy exists anywhere in cairosvg/; read_url's own docstring states the default fetcher has 'no limitations' (cairosvg/url.py:133-135)

defusedxml is used for the XML parse with forbid_entities/forbid_external defaulting to True unless unsafe=True is passed (cairosvg/parser.py:390-392) - that is XXE containment, not an SSRF sanitizer, and the unsafe flag is caller-controlled
The only structural mitigation available to integrators is injecting a restrictive url_fetcher (cairosvg/parser.py:354); the library itself performs no validation on fetched URLs
parse_url's file-branch (cairosvg/url.py:101-124) only resolves relative references against the document base; it neither restricts nor validates the resulting scheme/host
inputBoundaryInventory.nonVulnerabilityNote: Tree(url='#...') fragment references and helpers.py:47 / text.py:71 parse_url(...).fragment reads stay inside the current document (fragment-only) and do not trigger a fetch by themselves; the extract_url/parse_url rows covering those sites are candidates for Step 3 labeling, not presumed vulnerabilities. Similarly, kwargs['url'] = options.input in the CLI passes a locally-typed filename/URL argument chosen by the operator running the converter.

extraction.executionPlan: codeql query run (sequential, one query at a time) followed by codeql bqrs decode --format=csv; NOT database analyze / SARIF. No CodeQL execution in this step - queries are generated only.
extraction.metadataForm: plain multi-column select queries carrying @name/@description/@id only; intentionally no @kind problem (wrong shape for multi-column candidate tables) and no @kind table (not assumed to exist). Raw BQRS output is decoded directly to CSV.
columnContract: node (location-backed AST node; decodes as file:line:col)
arg_index (0-based positional argument index, -1 when not applicable)
match_kind ('api' = resolved real API call via API graphs, 'ast' = syntax-level match)

matchKindSemantics.api: call resolved through semmle.python.ApiGraphs (API::moduleImport(...).getMember(...).getACall()); only genuine resolved calls into external modules (urllib.request.urlopen / Request / urlretrieve)
matchKindSemantics.ast: pure AST shape match (callee name text, receiver name, string-literal keyword/argument values); used for all internal cairosvg wrappers and content-derived reads, because defusedxml/tinycss2/cssselect2/PIL/cairocffi sources are not part of the database and their members cannot be resolved through API graphs

exclusions: test files excluded by the isTestPath filter: cairosvg/test_api.py and test_non_regression/ (matches '%test%')
the nested CairoSVG-db CodeQL database directory inside the source tree is excluded from source scanning; it contains no .py files so it cannot contribute AST rows
setup.py is packaging metadata only; no candidate shapes occur in it
ground-truth files shipped in the tree (CVE-Report-CairoSVG-SSRF.md, ssrf_sinks.csv, ssrf_sinks.json, ssrf_vulnerability_report.md) were neither opened nor scanned

uncoveredCases: Tree(**kwargs) (cairosvg/parser.py:343): bytestring/file_obj/url enter through a kwargs dict, so no individual Parameter AST nodes exist for them; mitigated by the entry-function parameter rows (svg2*/convert) and the Tree(url=...) keyword rows on the sink side

Node dict attribute flow: cairosvg/parser.py:190 self.update(self.xml_tree.attrib) copies input XML attributes into a dict subclass and parser.py:312-313/cairosvg/image.py:24 read them back via dict.get; dict update/get taint transfer is not tracked by extraction-level data flow, so the .get('href')-family rows are syntax-level evidence at the read sites

cairosvg/url.py:143 'return url_fetcher(url, resource_type)' - the fetcher is a callable stored in a local/attribute; the dispatch target (default fetch) is not statically resolvable. The call is captured as an ast row, and fetch/read_url/Node.fetch_url definitions are captured as wrapper_param rows

cairosvg/__main__.py:72 'kwargs['url'] = options.input' - propagation into the kwargs dict literal is not dataflow-tracked at extraction level; the options.input attribute read and the Surface.convert/Tree url parameters are captured on both sides of the boundary instead
third-party members unreachable by API graphs: ElementTree.fromstring (defusedxml), tinycss2.parse_* , Image.open (PIL), cssselect2 wrappers - matched at ast level only (callee name + receiver name)

cairosvg/css.py:21 TODO 'pass href for relative URLs' - <style> element content is parsed without an element-specific base URL; relative @import resolution uses the document-level url argument passed into parse_stylesheets (cairosvg/parser.py:395)

keyword-only parameters have no positional index; rows for them use arg_index = -1 with the parameter name in the callable/notes context (Function.getArgByName covers both positional and keyword-only parameters)
